topics.topic: A10 concurrency coverage and references for connection-change races
questions: Must the concurrency outcome now reference A5 and M01 because a connection can change while the running service is admitting or executing scan, placement, and mark operations?
After A5 introduces live record rereading and changes that can race with scan, placement and mark, must the concurrency category reference A5 and state the snapshot or recheck outcome?
Does the concurrency review also cover A5's newly introduced race between each operation and a live change to the connection record, and if so why is A5 not referenced?

quotes:
The service reads the connection record at each scan, placement and mark, so a change
   applies from the next operation without a restart.
- concurrency: APPLICABLE; references: A3, A4, A6; affected: M04, M07
judgement.divergence: An in-progress operation either continues from the connection it already read or rechecks and refuses after a concurrent change; the calling flow and owner notice whether files are processed or effects are written.
judgement.why: The new live-read rule makes connection-change concurrency observable but does not define which side of an in-progress operation a concurrent change affects.

basis:

   applies from the next operation without a restart.

When the agent later
changes the root or a subfolder it clears the confirmation in the same write, and sets it again
after the owner confirms the new folders (R0-11).

topics.topic: Authoritative camera timestamp, timezone interpretation, and fallback criteria
questions: Which camera timestamp field is authoritative, how is a camera time with no zone interpreted as a UTC instant, and what makes a camera record unusable so that modification time is used?

quotes:
The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time. `DateTimeOriginal` uses `OffsetTimeOriginal` when that offset has
   the form `+HH:MM` or `-HH:MM`; otherwise it is read in the configured time zone, and so is
   `DateTime`. A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.

A camera
   time with no offset is read in the configured time zone. A local time that occurs twice is the
   first occurrence, and a local time that does not exist is read with the offset in force before
   the clock change. A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
judgement.why: A2 specifies field precedence, offset handling, the configured-zone interpretation, ambiguous and nonexistent local times, and every fallback criterion.
